answer: A mechanism that actually bites: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because meadow only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, marble is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any vine approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
